x.name: Modal
x.bio:
AI infrastructure that developers love 💚

Run inference, sandboxes, batch processing, training, and many other things on Modal

tweets.text: We demonstrate stable and correct training by reproducing Training Search Agents with GRPO by @lu__jasper, which trains gpt-oss-20b to perform multi-turn agentic search over a corpus of SEC filings with keyword-matching, grep, and read tools. https://t.co/W1v3ayyWNx

Tinker changed how people do post-training. We're big fans, and so are many of the teams we work with. But as those teams scale up, they keep raising the same two problems: per-token pricing gets expensive quickly, and you’re limited to the models and features the provider decides to support.

We think a good API deserves more than one implementation.

Today we're releasing Spindle, an open-source, Tinker-compatible training server that runs in your Modal workspace. Your existing Tinker scripts run unchanged, and because you own the server, you pay for GPU time instead of tokens.

tweets.text:
The era of vibe hacking is here.

@morphllm’s DeepSeek V4.1 abliterated is pretty phenomenal too, but you do have to sign up and get approval before you can use it!

I strongly believe a part of why so many critical vulnerabilities are happening all over the proliferation of "abliterated" models, or models with safeguards removed.

You can access an abliterated GLM 5.3, a near frontier AI model, on @abliteration_ai today. And it's a world class penetration tester for like $10.

Some people are misreading this to mean that it is specific to finding a known CVE exploit like a script kiddie and being dismissive.

No, I literally mean you can point certain models to any website and say “figure out the vulnerabilities”. I don’t have evidence that it can find be zero days with this approach, but it can definitely do some serious damage, replicate CVEs, and find way more security flaws in 5 mins than a world class security researcher
